key_insight: The study directly observes Kelvin-wave turbulence on a single vortex filament, confirming a weak-turbulence cascade driven by six-wave interactions.
engineering_relevance: This provides an experimental basis for modeling energy transport and dissipation along vortex cores in classical and quantum turbulent flows.
method: High-resolution spatiotemporal measurements of a single vortex filament
Resolved Kelvin-wave motion across a broad range of scales
Compared measured spectra with weak-turbulence predictions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports wave-amplitude spectra consistent with the predicted cascade and identifies six-wave resonant interactions as the transfer mechanism.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated under controlled single-filament conditions, so extending them to complex multi-vortex or strongly forced flows may require caution.
paper_title: Experimental evidence of Kelvin wave turbulence along a vortex core
